gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, on Thinkware's US store, the U3000 is "Not compatible with the LTE Module" while the U3000 Pro is sold with one, or that the add-on Radar Module (TWA-RADS, $89.99) used by the U1000 Plus and ARC 900 does not detect people walking by and keeps a clip only when an impact follows the radar wake-up, whereas the U3000 and U3000 Pro have built-in front and rear radar that records on motion.
standout_why: I opened these cited pages: Thinkware's RADAR Parking Mode FAQ, which covers only the U3000 and U3000 Pro; thinkwarestore.com/parking-mode, which says only "U1000 Plus and Q1000: Optional Radar Module" and describes motion clips in general; the U3000 Pro US store page; and the Digital Camera World U3000 Pro review, which says the camera starts recording when it detects motion and mentions neither the U1000 nor the add-on module. I also opened the uncited Dash Cam Empire U1000 vs U3000 page, which never mentions an external radar for the U1000. None of these pages mentions the U3000's LTE exclusion, or that the add-on module ignores pedestrians and needs an impact before it keeps a clip. ChatGPT's second answer marked 'Optional LTE connectivity: Yes' for the U3000, which the maker's store contradicts. Its first answer listed the U1000 Plus as a radar-parking 'modular alternative' without these limits. I did not open the cited Tom's Guide review.
decides: This confirms the Thinkware U3000 Pro as the pick and changes the order behind it. The U3000 at $479.99 is the value pick only for shoppers who do not want remote alerts, because it cannot take the LTE module (the U3000 Pro + LTE bundle is $689.99). The U1000 Plus, and the ARC 900 + RADAR bundle at $509.99, drop out of a radar-parking shortlist: their external module does not wake for pedestrians, the people who key or break into cars, and saves nothing unless an impact follows. DDPAI's N5 Dual 2026 radar kit is the only DDPAI option. I could not open its maker page to check how its radar behaves, so its place in the top three depends on angles that can read store.ddpai.com.

findings.label: LTE module compatibility
findings.value: Not compatible with the LTE Module
findings.note: This line is printed as a heading directly under the price, above 'Select option'. The page has no LTE variant; its variants are Front & Rear $479.99, + iVolt Mini $799.99 and + iVolt Xtra $949.99.

findings.label: Price and radar
findings.value: $479.99 (was $549.99); built-in front and rear radar; OBD II power cable in the box, no hardwiring cable
findings.note: Sale tag, no stock notice. The page says: 'Radar Parking Mode uses low-power front and rear radars to monitor motion' and 'Requires hardwiring or the OBD-II cable.' It gives no exact front or rear resolution in the text.

findings.label: LTE compatibility and price
findings.value: Front & Rear $549.99 (was $579.99); Front & Rear + LTE Module $689.99; the LTE module and the infrared cabin camera cannot be used at the same time
findings.source_title: U3000 PRO Front & Rear | 4K & 2K Dash Cam | THINKWARE
findings.note: SKUs TW-U3000PRODO and TW-U3000PRODO-LTE. Sale tag, no stock or dispatch notice.

findings.label: Channels, sensors, storage, parking power
findings.value: 2-channel (front + rear). Front: 3840×2160 at 30 fps or 2560×1440 at 60 fps, Sony STARVIS 2 IMX678. Rear: 2560×1440 at 30 fps, Sony STARVIS 2 IMX675. 64 GB microSD included, 512 GB max. OBD II power cable included. Built-in radar, supercapacitor and GPS.
findings.source_title: U3000 PRO Front & Rear | 4K & 2K Dash Cam | THINKWARE
findings.note: The page gives per-channel modes but does not say whether 60 fps on the front holds while the rear also records. iVolt Xtra battery: $369.99.

findings.label: Radar parking mode: maker-stated models, power need and exclusions
findings.value: Only the U3000 PRO and U3000 are listed. Hardwiring or an OBD II cable is required. Range adjustable from 1 m to 5 m in 5 levels, measured from the rear camera. Designed for movement slower than 20 km/h (12 mph). THINKWARE Connected features are unavailable in RADAR Parking Mode.
findings.source_title: RADAR Parking Mode – Thinkware Help Center
findings.note: Further exclusions: a rear camera on a trunk window may not detect properly; metallic UV tint films and other 24 GHz products can interfere; 'Not every object is guaranteed to be detected.' This is a cited rival page, so these points are not new.

findings.label: Compatibility and price
findings.value: $89.99; 'Compatible with U1000 Plus, U1000, Q1000, and X1000'; parking surveillance requires a hardwiring cable or OBD II power cable
findings.note: Footnote on the same page: 'Energy Saving Mode 2.0 will disable all THINKWARE CLOUD features.' The page does not list the U3000 or U3000 Pro, which have radar built in.

findings.label: What it detects and what it saves
findings.value: 'Sedan or greater sized vehicle can be detected.' 'People passing by will not be detected.' When motion is detected the camera readies itself, then saves a 20 s clip (10 s before, 10 s after) only if an impact is detected; with no impact it discards the footage and returns to Energy Saving Mode 2.0. Detection about 7 m, about 80° horizontal and 35° vertical.
findings.note: The two quoted product-note lines are verbatim. I paraphrased the impact-only behaviour from the Description; its closing sentence reads 'When no impacts are detected, the dash cam does not save the footage and resumes Energy Saving Mode 2.0.' Metal objects near the mirror or ADAS sensors can stop detection.

findings.label: Radar trigger behaviour (named reviewer)
findings.value: Digital Camera World: 'If motion is detected in that zone, to the front or rear, the U3000 Pro fires into life and starts recording'; the default sensitivity woke the camera for rainfall and recorded 'a few dozen clips of rainfall in a single night'
findings.source_title: Thinkware U3000 Pro review – Digital Camera World
findings.note: The reviewer says turning sensitivity down one notch helped. The review quotes $499 US, an older figure; use the store's $549.99 read today. This is a cited rival page.

findings.label: Radar, price, stock and channels
findings.value: 'External Radar Module (Optional)'. Front & Rear $369.99 (+ iVolt Mini $649.99, + iVolt Xtra $799.99); no radar bundle. Page shows 'Out of Stock'. 2-channel: front 4K at 30 fps or 2K at 60 fps (Sony STARVIS IMX515), rear 1080p at 30 fps (2 MP). microSD 32 to 512 GB, 64 GB included, hardwiring cable included.
findings.source_title: U1000 Plus Front & Rear | THINKWARE US
findings.note: The page shows 'Out of Stock' near the top but also an Add to cart button, so stock is unclear. No sale banner. A radar setup costs $369.99 + $89.99 for the module = $459.99 at Thinkware US list prices today.

findings.label: Radar bundle, compatibility and price
findings.value: ARC 900 Front & Rear + RADAR Module $509.99 (TW-ARC900D-RAD); base $419.99; + LTE $569.99; + LTE + RADAR $659.99. 'External Radar Module (Optional)'. Front 3840×2160 at 30 fps or 2560×1440 at 60 fps; rear 2560×1440 at 30 fps. Hardwiring cable included.
findings.source_title: ARC 900 Front & Rear + RADAR Module | THINKWARE US
findings.note: The page describes the radar as waking the camera from sleep and saving a 20 s clip (10 s before and after) when an impact occurs. This is the same external-module behaviour as TWA-RADS. No discount shown. ChatGPT got no result for this model.

findings.label: Radar kit variant (partner store read)
findings.value: 'N5 Dual 2026 + Radar Accessory (Radar+ OBD & hardwire Kit)' $269.00 (list $279.00), against N5 Dual 2026 alone at $189.00 and + Hardwire Kit at $199.00; in stock
findings.source_title: N5 Dual 2026 4K Dash Cam – DDPAI store
findings.note: Figures come from the brief's partner-store read of 2026-11-21. My own reads of this page (storecheck and WebFetch) returned HTTP 429 every time, so I could not open the radar description. The radar kit ships with its own OBD hardwire kit in this variant. Code SAVEBIGBF takes a further 12% off until 2026-11-30, per the brief.
